chapter: Opening, arrival in Los Angeles and the Quality Four
title: Studying cornet with an Italian teacher arranged by his grandfather
summary: Howard recalls an Italian cornet teacher, set up by his grandfather, who drilled him in classical technique; he cannot remember the teacher's name.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Learning your horn: teachers, lessons and fees

blocks.x: So, now, when you started as a musician, did you study with a teacher from the beginning or were you one of those natural talented people who just picked it
Oh, no, I was fortunate to have an Italian teacher.
Did you start on piano or anything like that in the beginning?
No, I started on -- what did I start playing on? I happen to forget, now. It's been a long time. I played on -- oh, I can't remember.
Did you ever play piano as a young man?
Oh, yeah, sure, but not too much piano, because --
That wasn't the first instrument then.
No, my first instrument was a -- what do you call that?
Trumpet? (Coronet?)
Coronet, coronet, coronet.
And that's what you studied with the Italian teacher, huh?
An Italian teacher, yes. That's what I had.

So you had really, beginning, possibly more than a lot of the black musicians. What I've heard, a lot of the black musicians, possibly at that time and even later, didn't get a chance to get to the great teachers,

because of money or just depending on where they lived and everything like that. You understand, that they were unable to get to an A-1 teacher. From your father, is that right? Who set that up for you?
My grandfather.
Your grandfather. Because, like I said, a lot of them didn't have money (inaudible) musicians, they just had to get up as they would go.
Well, I didn't have any money, but when they started telling me just about how things are going, why, they got me started on the -- oh, what do you call that? What do you call that, Buddy?
How things are going with the music, you mean, or the lessons?
Yeah, with the music. When they got me started going, how things were going with the music, well, I naturally -- naturally gave me the right thing to hang onto.
The right studies?
Yeah, the right studies.
Well, in other words, you had to go through all the technical things, the tone studies, all the exercises.
I certainly did, yes.
The proper lessons. Yeah, well, I
I certainly did.
But then that was taking you more into the classical field, wasn't it, more into --

Yeah, going into the classical field, because of the way they were teaching me, you know. I had an Italian teacher and he was a (unintelligible). He was really something else. And you had to remember things that he told you.
I see. Do you remember his name?
Do you remember the name of your Italian teacher?
No, I don't. I can't remember his name. I'm sorry.
Was he playing with the symphony orchestra or was he a player also?
Yeah, he was a player.
So he was actually working in some band or doing some work while he was teaching you.
Yes.
